independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived rather than accepted. NUMBERING: Ps 50 is absent from the +1 and +2 membership lists and verse_map_web marks Ps.50.0 as mt='inside Ps.50.1', so the identity-psalm claim and the owner-ruled opening form web:Ps.50.0 = oshb:Ps.50.1 are both correct; oshb:Ps.50.1 does open מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ף before the divine-name stack, which is what 'sits inside MT verse 1' has to mean. BYTES: אֵ֤ל אֱֽלֹהִ֡ים יְֽהוָ֗ה collates at tier byte against oshb:Ps.50.1, and each of the 3 members collates byte separately, so the El reading is settled on pointed bytes rather than on a skeleton sweep - the short-token homography hazard for the unpointed form is correctly avoided here, and the three-word gloss covers the three quoted words. SELAH: the inventory carries exactly one Ps 50 entry, Ps.50.6 (1 verse), matching web_selah at web:Ps.50.6; the row uses it as a closing corroboration and does not lean on it as a driver, the same mark is used symmetrically across the 50:6|50:7 seam, and no absence claim is made anywhere. SEAM: the front edge is a psalm boundary and the back edge is tier-1 - third-person narration closes at וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ שָׁמַ֣יִם צִדְק֑וֹ and direct address opens the next verse with שִׁמְעָ֤ה עַמִּ֨י. TITLE LABELS: the superscription inventory gives Ps 50 exactly mizmor and le_asaph, matching device_notes. Observation (not filed): the row calls 50:1-6 third-person narration while quoting the first-person summons at web:Ps.50.5, but it discloses that as an 'embedded summons', so the description holds - the count built on that same verse across the seam does not, and I file it there. One defect stands here, in the collection framing.

challenges.claim: device_notes says the title opens ‘Book II's run of Asaph psalms’, but the device inventory records no run of Asaph psalms in Book II - Ps 50 is the only le-Asaph psalm there.
challenges.evidence: psalm_device_inventory genre_label_membership le_asaph = 12 psalms (unit: psalms): [50, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 82, 83]. five_books gives II = psalms 42-72 and III = psalms 73-89. Intersecting the two: 1 of the 12 le-Asaph psalms falls in Book II (Ps 50 itself) and 11 of the 12 fall in Book III, so the run is a Book III phenomenon and Ps 50 stands alone in Book II. The recoverable intended sense - that Ps 50 opens the 12-psalm le-Asaph corpus, and does so from inside Book II - is correct, which is why this is low and not a span challenge; as written the sentence attributes to Book II a run the inventory does not support. The superscription labels themselves check out: superscriptions/50 = {mizmor, le_asaph}, and oshb:Ps.50.1 opens מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ף.

reviews.reasoning: BYTES: אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֶ֣יךָ אָנֹֽכִי collates at tier byte against oshb:Ps.50.7 and the three-word gloss covers the three quoted words; שִׁמְעָ֤ה collates byte and is genuinely token 0 of the verse, so the 'opens with' claim is positionally true. The form claim on it survives the bytes as far as the staged extract can carry one (no morphology layer): no prefix consonant, and the paragogic he visible in the pointing, against the prefix forms elsewhere in the psalm. NUMBERING: Ps 50 is identity, so the row's bare oshb: refs need no dual-cite arithmetic and citation_sweep raises nothing. SELAH: the row cites Ps.50.6 - one verse outside its own front edge - explicitly as corroboration and explicitly 'not a driver', which is the permitted use; the inventory confirms exactly 1 Ps 50 selah, and the row across the same seam cites the same verse, Ps.50.6, so the pair is symmetric. SEAMS: both edges are tier-1 speech-frame facts - direct address opens at oshb:Ps.50.7 and the explicit dixit formula וְלָ֤רָשָׁ֨ע אָ֘מַ֤ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים opens oshb:Ps.50.16, so the back edge is not in doubt. Observation (not filed): the rationale calls web:Ps.50.14 'the positive instruction that closes it' while the span runs one verse further to web:Ps.50.15, and device_notes says the close is 50:14-15; the fields disagree about the closing unit but the seam itself is unaffected. The filed defect is the speech count, which is both unswept and, on the bytes, wrong.

challenges.claim: ‘the first of the psalm's 2 divine speeches (sweep: 2 speeches)’ dresses an interpretive count as a machine sweep over an object sweep.py cannot count, leaves the object undefined, and undercounts the psalm's first-person divine utterances, which the bytes put at 3.
challenges.evidence: There is no spelling, term, formula or root behind 'speeches', so no sweep.py run can produce the figure, and the mandated form - name the swept object first, then the digit with its unit - is not met. On the bytes the psalm carries a third first-person divine utterance before the two the row counts: oshb:Ps.50.5 is אִסְפוּ לִ֥י חֲסִידָ֑י - an imperative with the 1cs suffix on לִ֥י ('to me') and 1cs possession in חֲסִידָ֑י ('my faithful ones'), i.e. God speaking in the first person, which WEB also sets inside quotation marks at web:Ps.50.5: ““Gather my saints together to me, those who have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.””. A defensible object would be 'divine speeches introduced by an explicit speech formula' (2, unit: speech-frame openings: oshb:Ps.50.7 שִׁמְעָ֤ה עַמִּ֨י and oshb:Ps.50.16 וְלָ֤רָשָׁ֨ע אָ֘מַ֤ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים), which is what the row is actually describing; as written the figure is contradicted by the psalm's own embedded summons - the verse quoted by the row on the other side of this seam.

reviews.reasoning: The strongest row in the cluster and I can find no defect worth filing. BYTES: וְלָ֤רָשָׁ֨ע אָ֘מַ֤ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים collates at tier byte against oshb:Ps.50.16, it is genuinely verse-initial (tokens 0-2), and the gloss renders exactly those three words - quote and gloss cover the same span. The driver is a textbook tier-1 signal: an explicit narrator speech formula plus an addressee change, the highest-grade seam evidence available in this book, and it depends on no seg-layer or metadata claim. The back edge is the psalm's own end at web:Ps.50.23, so no rival seam exists there. NUMBERING: identity psalm, bare oshb: refs correct. MARKS: the paseq inventory lists Ps.50.16 and Ps.50.21, and the row makes 0 seg claims - correct restraint, since paseq is not quotable verse text; there is no selah in this span and no absence claim is made. WEB: all 3 of its quoted strings are verbatim, each with an inline web: ref (the cluster-wide check is clean over 28 quotes). The rejected_alternative is apt: it tests 50:22-23 as a separate close and rejects it on the continuing addressee, which is the right test given that 50:16 opens with a dixit formula and 50:22 does not. Two observations I decline to file. (1) The rationale says the 50:14/50:23 repetition frames 'the whole psalm', which it cannot - web:Ps.50.14 is mid-psalm and the opening thirteen verses lie outside any such frame - but device_notes states the accurate version, 'an inclusio internal to the psalm', and no seam rests on the stronger wording. (2) The repetition is exact in WEB English but not in Hebrew: oshb:Ps.50.14 has זְבַ֣ח לֵאלֹהִ֣ים תּוֹדָ֑ה (imperative, with the divine name intervening between the two members) against oshb:Ps.50.23 זֹבֵ֥חַ תּוֹדָ֗ה (participle, the two members contiguous). The row's claim is explicitly about the WEB phrase and is carried on web: refs, and the WEB rendering is faithful to both verses, so it is within the rules; naming the morphological difference would strengthen the inclusio argument, not weaken it.

NUMBERING re-derived first, since this is a +2 psalm: both oshb:Ps.51.1 and oshb:Ps.51.2 carry is_counted_title true and both map to web:Ps.51.0, and web:Ps.51.1 = oshb:Ps.51.3 through web:Ps.51.6 = oshb:Ps.51.8. All 4 dual-cites in the refs array are arithmetically correct, the two title pseudo-ref pairs are the owner-ruled form, and citation_sweep raises no problem. TITLE LABELS: superscriptions/51 = {mizmor, lamnatseach, le_david}, matching device_notes exactly; oshb:Ps.51.1 is לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד and the historical note is oshb:Ps.51.2. BYTES: לְךָ֤ לְבַדְּךָ֨ חָטָאתִי֮ collates at tier byte against oshb:Ps.51.6 and is genuinely verse-initial, so the fronting observation is sound; its gloss covers two of the three quoted words, leaving the verb unrendered, which I note here rather than file. The span is defensible - petition grounded in confession, no addressee change - and the rejected_alternative tests the obvious 51:2|51:3 rival on register. What fails is the lexical identification at oshb:Ps.51.4, wrong in the rationale and wrong again in the substrate signal, which then propagates across the 51:6|51:7 seam into the next row; the same verse is a K/Q verse quoted without disclosure, and one bookkeeping universal in device_notes is false against this psalm's own four rows.

challenges.claim: The row glosses הֶ֭רֶב as ‘(wash)’ and claims its root is reused in the next span's opening petition; both are false - the washing verb in that verse is כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי (root kbs) and הֶ֭רֶב belongs to a different root entirely.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.51.4 (= web:Ps.51.2) reads הרבה הֶ֭רֶב כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי מֵעֲוֺנִ֑י וּֽמֵחַטָּאתִ֥י טַהֲרֵֽנִי. The washing verb is כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי, root kbs, and the form the next span reuses is תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי at oshb:Ps.51.9 (= web:Ps.51.7) - the same root and the same 1cs suffix as כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי, differing only by the prefix consonant. הֶ֭רֶב is from rbb/rbh ('make much'), which is why WEB renders it adverbially inside “Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. Cleanse me from my sin.” (web:Ps.51.2) rather than as a second verb; its actual cognate in this psalm is כְּרֹ֥ב at oshb:Ps.51.3 (= web:Ps.51.1), one verse earlier. So the parenthetical gloss is wrong, and observed_substrate_signals[1] - that this token 'anticipates the same root's reuse in the next span's opening petition (51:7)' - is wrong in the same move: the root reused at web:Ps.51.7 = oshb:Ps.51.9 is kbs, carried by a token this row never quotes. Both quotes collate at tier byte, so this is a semantic misidentification of correctly-spliced bytes, not a quotation defect. The identical misidentification is installed on the far side of the 51:6|51:7 seam, so the repair is one edit authored once and applied to both rows.

challenges.claim: oshb:Ps.51.4 is a ketiv/qere verse and the row quotes the pointed member as if it were plain verse text, with no K/Q disclosure anywhere in the row.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json kq carries Ps.51.4 (1 note; the book inventory is 68 notes over 65 verses). The staged bytes serialize the pair unpointed-then-pointed: oshb:Ps.51.4 begins הרבה הֶ֭רֶב, which is the pattern the extract uses at every other K/Q verse I sampled - oshb:Ps.9.13 עניים עֲנָוִֽים, oshb:Ps.10.10 ודכה יִדְכֶּ֥ה, oshb:Ps.18.51 מגדל מַגְדִּיל֮. The row quotes only the pointed member and presents it as the verse's reading, so a reader cannot tell from the row that the token is one side of a K/Q pair - which also matters for the gloss, since the two members are not the same form. Disclosure is mandatory when a K/Q verse is quoted; the same undisclosed token is quoted again across the 51:6|51:7 seam, so this repair installs on both rows.

challenges.claim: ‘before the imperative register resumes at the next seam’ is contradicted by the bytes at the seam it names - the next span opens with prefix-conjugation forms, not imperatives.
challenges.evidence: The next span opens at web:Ps.51.7 = oshb:Ps.51.9: תְּחַטְּאֵ֣נִי בְאֵז֣וֹב וְאֶטְהָ֑ר תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי וּמִשֶּׁ֥לֶג אַלְבִּֽין. Its two petition verbs, תְּחַטְּאֵ֣נִי and תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי, both carry the taw preformative and are prefix-conjugation forms used volitively, which WEB renders with English imperatives. The minimal pair is decisive because it is the same root and suffix on both sides of the seam: oshb:Ps.51.4 כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי (no preformative) against oshb:Ps.51.9 תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי. The first imperative-form token in that span is הַסְתֵּ֣ר at oshb:Ps.51.11 = web:Ps.51.9, two WEB verses past the seam. The seam at 51:6|51:7 survives on register - volitive petition does resume there, against the indicative of oshb:Ps.51.8 הֵן אֱ֭מֶת חָפַ֣צְתָּ - so this is a warrant-precision defect, not a span challenge; the word 'imperative' is the part that cannot be sustained on the pointed text.

challenges.claim: device_notes' claim that ‘this +2 psalm's rows dual-cite both MT title verses throughout’ is an unswept universal and is false for three of the psalm's four rows.
challenges.evidence: check_universals flags the token 'throughout' in this field as a universal with no adjacent digit-bearing count. Re-derived: the rows covering this psalm tile web:Ps.51.1-Ps.51.19 exactly - check_tiling over that range reports 19 of 19 verses covered with no gap, overlap or order problem - so no further rows for this psalm can exist without an overlap; of those 4 rows, exactly 1 carries oshb:Ps.51.1 and oshb:Ps.51.2 in its refs, this one, and 3 carry neither (unit: rows). That is also the correct policy behaviour, since the title pairs with the opening row, which is why this is low: the practice is right and only the sentence describing it is wrong.

reviews.reasoning: The span is right and much of what is asserted about it is not. NUMBERING: web:Ps.51.7 = oshb:Ps.51.9, web:Ps.51.8 = oshb:Ps.51.10, web:Ps.51.10 = oshb:Ps.51.12, web:Ps.51.2 = oshb:Ps.51.4 - all 4 dual-cites are correct +2 arithmetic, and citation_sweep is clean. BYTES: all 5 Hebrew runs in the row (4 distinct strings) collate at tier byte, so nothing here is a splicing failure; every defect below is a claim made about correctly-spliced bytes. The unit itself is defensible - web:Ps.51.7-12 is a continuous block addressed to God with no vocative or addressee change, and its back edge at 51:12|51:13 is a real register shift - so I do not contest the span. I contest both quantified device claims, the lexical identification carried over from the 51:6|51:7 seam, and the positional claim at oshb:Ps.51.12. Worth noting for the gate: the universals check passes this row's superlative only because a digit sits beside it, and the digit is the thing that is wrong.

challenges.claim: The row identifies הֶ֭רֶב as the wash-root and says תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי reuses ‘the root already quoted at 51:2’; the reused root is kbs, carried by כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי, a token neither row quotes.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.51.4 (= web:Ps.51.2) reads הרבה הֶ֭רֶב כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי מֵעֲוֺנִ֑י וּֽמֵחַטָּאתִ֥י טַהֲרֵֽנִי. תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי at oshb:Ps.51.9 (= web:Ps.51.7) shares root and 1cs suffix with כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי, differing only by the taw preformative; הֶ֭רֶב is from rbb/rbh and its cognate in this psalm is כְּרֹ֥ב at oshb:Ps.51.3 (= web:Ps.51.1). So observed_substrate_signals[0], 'repeats the wash-root of oshb:Ps.51.4's הֶ֭רֶב', is false, and the rationale's 'reuses the root already quoted at 51:2' is false in a second way - the root that is reused was never the token quoted at web:Ps.51.2. The underlying literary observation, that a washing verb straddles the 51:6|51:7 seam, is correct and is this row's best continuity argument; it is attached to the wrong word. Separately, oshb:Ps.51.4 is a K/Q verse (pmarks kq Ps.51.4, 1 note) whose bytes serialize the pair unpointed-then-pointed, הרבה הֶ֭רֶב, and this row quotes the pointed member with no K/Q disclosure - the same undisclosed quotation as on the near side of the seam, so one authored cure covers both rows.

challenges.claim: device_notes' ‘sweep: 6 imperatives across 6 verses (purify, wash, let me hear, hide, create, renew)’ is contradicted by the pointed text: three of the six named forms are prefix-conjugation, and two genuine imperatives in the span are omitted.
challenges.evidence: Verse by verse over the span, dual-cited: oshb:Ps.51.9 = web:Ps.51.7 תְּחַטְּאֵ֣נִי בְאֵז֣וֹב וְאֶטְהָ֑ר תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי וּמִשֶּׁ֥לֶג אַלְבִּֽין - 'purify' is תְּחַטְּאֵ֣נִי and 'wash' is תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי, both taw-preformative prefix forms, not imperatives; oshb:Ps.51.10 = web:Ps.51.8 opens תַּ֭שְׁמִיעֵנִי, likewise taw-preformative, so 'let me hear' is not an imperative either; oshb:Ps.51.11 = web:Ps.51.9 הַסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נֶיךָ מֵחֲטָאָ֑י וְֽכָל עֲוֺ֖נֹתַ֣י מְחֵֽה carries TWO imperative-form tokens, הַסְתֵּ֣ר and מְחֵֽה, of which the list takes only the first; oshb:Ps.51.12 = web:Ps.51.10 carries בְּרָא and חַדֵּ֥שׁ, both imperative forms, correctly listed; oshb:Ps.51.13 = web:Ps.51.11 has אַל תַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥נִי and אַל תִּקַּ֥ח, negated prefix forms, correctly excluded; oshb:Ps.51.14 = web:Ps.51.12 opens הָשִׁ֣יבָה, an imperative with paragogic he, which the list omits. Re-derived: 5 imperative-form tokens in the span (unit: tokens) - הַסְתֵּ֣ר, מְחֵֽה, בְּרָא, חַדֵּ֥שׁ, הָשִׁ֣יבָה - not 6, and they sit in 3 of the 6 verses, not across all 6. The minimal pair proving the prefix forms are not imperatives is inside this psalm: oshb:Ps.51.4 כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי against oshb:Ps.51.9 תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי, same root, same suffix, differing by the preformative. The same error reaches the rationale, which calls web:Ps.51.12 = oshb:Ps.51.14 'the climactic double imperative': that verse is הָשִׁ֣יבָה לִּ֭י שְׂשׂ֣וֹן יִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וְר֖וּחַ נְדִיבָ֣ה תִסְמְכֵֽנִי - one imperative (הָשִׁ֣יבָה) plus one prefix form (תִסְמְכֵֽנִי), not two imperatives. The staged extract has no morphology layer, so these are argued from the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings, which is the same basis available to the writer.

challenges.claim: ‘this psalm's highest imperative concentration by that count’ is false: web:Ps.51.1-2 carries as many imperative-form tokens in 2 verses as this span does in 6.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.51.3 = web:Ps.51.1 reads חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱלֹהִ֣ים כְּחַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ מְחֵ֣ה פְשָׁעָֽי, giving imperative forms חָנֵּ֣נִי and מְחֵ֣ה; oshb:Ps.51.4 = web:Ps.51.2 reads הרבה הֶ֭רֶב כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי מֵעֲוֺנִ֑י וּֽמֵחַטָּאתִ֥י טַהֲרֵֽנִי, giving הֶ֭רֶב (the pointed K/Q member, Hiphil imperative of rbh), כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי and טַהֲרֵֽנִי. That is 5 imperative-form tokens across 2 WEB verses (unit: tokens per WEB verse = 2.5), or 4 across 2 verses = 2.0 if the K/Q token is set aside as contested. This span re-derives to 5 tokens across 6 WEB verses = 0.83 per verse, and even on the row's own figure of 6 it is 1.0 per verse. The superlative therefore fails on the row's own arithmetic as well as on mine, whichever way the K/Q question is taken.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals[1] says oshb:Ps.51.12 ‘opens with the verb’ בְּרָא - it does not - and then has that verse anticipate a root voiced ‘at Ps.51.10’, which under the row's own arithmetic is the same verse.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.51.12 reads לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא לִ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְר֥וּחַ נָ֝כ֗וֹן חַדֵּ֥שׁ בְּקִרְבִּֽי: tokens 0-1 are לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר and the verb בְּרָא is token 2, so the verse opens with its fronted object - which is the interesting fact, and the one the row's own rationale states correctly when it quotes לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא. Second defect in the same sentence: a bare ref is WEB numbering by convention, and the row's own refs array records 'web:Ps.51.10 = oshb:Ps.51.12', so 'the same root already voiced as a petition object at Ps.51.10' points at the very verse the signal is about. As written the signal has oshb:Ps.51.12 anticipating itself; there is no earlier occurrence of that root in this psalm for it to refer to.

challenges.claim: ‘the psalm's 4 internal seams (sweep: 4 row boundaries)’ miscounts the internal seams as 4 when there are 3, names a count object no sweep can produce, and states the chunking artifact inside row prose.
challenges.evidence: The rows covering this psalm tile web:Ps.51.1-Ps.51.19 exactly - check_tiling over that range reports 19 of 19 verses covered with no gap, overlap or order problem across 4 rows (unit: rows), whose starts are web:Ps.51.1, web:Ps.51.7, web:Ps.51.13, web:Ps.51.18. Four rows yield 3 internal seams (51:6|51:7, 51:12|51:13, 51:17|51:18); the outer edges are psalm boundaries, not internal seams. The parenthetical then swaps the object mid-sentence, counting 'row boundaries' to support a figure claimed for 'internal seams', and neither is an object sweep.py can count - there is no spelling, term, formula or root behind it. Separately, 'row boundaries' is chunking-artifact vocabulary in row prose, where cross-row reference must be verse-anchored; the row does this correctly elsewhere with 'the seam at 51:6|51:7'.

challenges.claim: Quote and gloss do not cover the same span: לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא is glossed ‘a clean heart create for me’, but ‘for me’ renders לִ֣י, which lies outside the quoted bytes.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.51.12 = web:Ps.51.10 reads לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא לִ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְר֥וּחַ נָ֝כ֗וֹן חַדֵּ֥שׁ בְּקִרְבִּֽי. The quoted run is tokens 0-2, לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא (collates at tier byte), while the gloss renders tokens 0-3, taking in לִ֣י. The cure is to re-cut one side: extending the quote to לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא לִ֣י matches the existing gloss and stays byte-true, or truncating the gloss to 'a clean heart create' matches the existing quote. Low because the argument does not turn on the extra word, but the parity rule binds glosses in both directions.

Token by token: צִיּ֑וֹן is the object of the first colon ('Zion'), תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה is the taw-preformative verb opening the second colon ('you build'), and 'the walls of Jerusalem' is חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם - tokens 5-6, outside the quoted run. The quoted pair therefore splices across the verse's internal division: the atnach (U+0591) sits on צִיּ֑וֹן, so the row has joined the last word of colon A to the first word of colon B and glossed the result as the two words it left out. The quote collates at tier byte, so this is a gloss failure over correct bytes, not a splicing failure - and because the same string and the same gloss recur in observed_substrate_signals[0], the row states it twice. The recoverable point - that this verse alone names the city and its walls - is true and survives a correct re-cut to חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם.
